context.objective: Document how we carry out Investment Purchases: Recording, Setup & Controls, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we open the investment purchase and assign people responsible for the checks. That is done by: Assigned investment/accounting preparer. What we do: open the New Investment Set Up and purchase-control checklists; record fund/entity, issuer/portfolio company, security type, purchase/closing date, cost/funding amount, counterparty, and payment date; assign preparer, second reviewer, callback/Treasury, compliance/screening, and approval roles; identify whether the investment is equity, debt, SAFE/note conversion, non-cash restructuring, fund-of-funds, or another supported category. Next, we collect and validate the deal document package. That is done by: Investment/accounting preparer; reviewer checks completeness. What we do: collect the complete deal “bible.” FA09-SC-06 System constraint A system, workbook, template, checklist, prior deliverable, or employee recollection is only a method, data source, or supporting record. It does not set a governing rule unless the source explicitly establishes an; confirm the approved investment, legal entities, security, shares/units, cost, closing date, payment terms, and restrictions; confirm the package includes capitalization table, structure chart, certificates/evidence of ownership, and required conversion/restructuring support; log missing/final-versus-draft documents and obtain them before the dependent step.
What event or incoming information prompts you to open the investment purchase, and how do you receive it?

After that, we complete and review the Investment Attribute Form. That is done by: Investment/accounting preparer; client provides/approves missing. What we do: record the investment name and portfolio-company name exactly as approved for the schedule of investments (SOI) and capital notices; record closing date, industry, security type, shares/units, and cost lines; record FAS 157 Level and client signer; compare every attribute to the supporting document or written client direction; resolve missing or conflicting attributes before system setup. Then, we document client or GP approval and clear counterparty checks. That is done by: Client/GP approves; Treasury/  and compliance roles clear. What we do: retain client/GP approval of purchase, amount, counterparty, and payment; validate new counterparty bank details using callback; apply Exiger screening when the jurisdiction meets the approved high-risk criteria; resolve any bank/screening discrepancy or escalation; confirm payment date and bank cut-off feasibility.
What happens to the purchase payment while a bank-detail or screening discrepancy remains unresolved?

Once that is done, we create Allvue issuer and security master data. That is done by: Investment/accounting preparer; second reviewer checks. What we do: in Allvue NAV, create or validate the Issuer; create the Security with the approved type and attributes; create the Lot using approved closing, share/unit, and cost information; create/apply the approved Allocation rule; in Allvue CRM, update Firm Known As, Industry, and FAS 157 Level; compare system fields to the Attribute Form. Following that, we prepare and approve the cash entry. That is done by: Investment/accounting preparer; cash-entry approval routes to all AFCs,. What we do: prepare the Daily Posting cash entry: DR Investment Payable 20080 / CR the correct Bank account; use an entry description distinct from the later cost entry; attach client approval, callback/screening evidence, deal/payment support, and calculation; route the entry to all AFCs, FCs, and Directors as specified by the source; resolve review comments and obtain required approvals.
Once the cash entry has the required approvals, what happens to it?

Following that, we release payment and confirm bank execution. That is done by: Treasury/  role executes; preparer coordinates. What we do: submit the approved payment through the treasury workflow; confirm release occurs sufficiently before the applicable bank cut-off; record payment status, bank settlement date (value date), bank reference, and any rejection/return; compare actual cash disbursed to the approved cash entry. Following that, we prepare and approve the cost entry. That is done by: Investment/accounting preparer; cost-entry approval routes to FCs and. What we do: confirm final acquisition cost and any supported non-cash component; prepare the General Operations entry: DR Investment – Acquisition 11010 / CR Investment Payable 20080; use a description different from the cash entry; attach final documents, Attribute Form, setup evidence, and cost support; route the entry to FCs and Directors, resolve comments, and post after approval.
After approval, how is the cash entry posted, and what tells the preparer it has posted successfully?

topics.answer: Investment Purchases: Recording, Setup & Controls
The initiating event that causes the preparer to open the investment setup and purchase-control checklists is not established.
The observable condition that demonstrates the overall investment-purchase work is complete is not established.

The assigned investment/accounting preparer performs setup and package collection and validation; review, callback/Treasury, compliance/screening and approval roles are assigned.
The role accountable for the overall investment-purchase process/result is not established.

The assigned investment/accounting preparer opens the New Investment Set Up and purchase-control checklists. They record fund/entity, issuer/portfolio company, security type, purchase/closing date, cost/funding amount, counterparty and payment date, and assign preparer, second reviewer, callback/Treasury, compliance/screening and approval roles.
During package collection, the preparer logs missing documents and whether documents are final or draft, then obtains missing/final documents before the dependent step.
The investment/accounting preparer completes the Investment Attribute Form; the client provides or approves missing information. Names are recorded exactly as approved for the SOI and capital notices, alongside closing date, industry, security type, shares/units, cost lines, FAS 157 Level and client signer. Attributes are compared to supporting documents or written client direction, and missing or conflicting attributes are resolved before system setup.
Client or GP approval of the purchase, amount, counterparty and payment is retained. New counterparty bank details are validated by callback; Exiger screening applies when the jurisdiction meets approved high-risk criteria. Bank or screening discrepancies and escalations are resolved, and payment date and bank cut-off feasibility are confirmed.
After the approval and counterparty-check stage, the investment/accounting preparer creates or validates the Issuer in Allvue NAV, creates the Security with approved type and attributes, creates the Lot using approved closing, share/unit and cost information, and creates/applies the approved Allocation rule. In Allvue CRM the preparer updates Firm Known As, Industry and FAS 157 Level; a second reviewer checks, and system fields are compared to the Attribute Form.
Following master-data setup, the preparer prepares the Daily Posting cash entry: debit Investment Payable 20080 and credit the correct bank account, using a description distinct from the later cost entry. Client approval, callback/screening evidence, deal/payment support and calculation are attached; the entry is routed to all AFCs, FCs and Directors as specified by the source, review comments are resolved and required approvals obtained.
Following cash-entry approval, the preparer coordinates submission of the approved payment through the treasury workflow; the Treasury role executes it. Release is confirmed sufficiently before the applicable bank cut-off.
Payment status, bank settlement date (value date), bank reference and any rejection or return are recorded; actual cash disbursed is compared with the approved cash entry.
Following payment release and bank execution confirmation, the investment/accounting preparer confirms final acquisition cost and any supported non-cash component and prepares the General Operations cost entry: debit Investment – Acquisition 11010 and credit Investment Payable 20080. The entry has a different description from the cash entry, is routed to FCs and Directors, and is posted after approval and resolution of comments.

The investment/accounting preparer collects and validates the deal document package; a reviewer checks completeness. The preparer confirms the approved investment, legal entities, security, shares/units, cost, closing date, payment terms and restrictions, and checks for the capitalization table, structure chart, certificates/evidence of ownership, and required conversion/restructuring support.
Each investment attribute is compared to supporting documents or written client direction; missing or conflicting attributes must be resolved before system setup.
Client/GP approves the purchase, amount, counterparty and payment; Treasury and compliance roles clear counterparty checks. New bank details are validated by callback, and qualifying high-risk jurisdictions receive Exiger screening; discrepancies or escalations are resolved.
The payment's status while a bank-detail or screening discrepancy remains unresolved was not established.
A second reviewer checks master-data setup, with system fields compared against the Attribute Form. Cash-entry review comments are resolved and required approvals obtained after routing to all AFCs, FCs and Directors as specified by the source.
Actual cash disbursed is compared with the approved cash entry; payment status, settlement date, bank reference and any rejection or return are recorded.
The cost entry is routed to FCs and Directors, comments are resolved, and the entry is posted after approval.

Category-specific changes to purchase steps or controls remain unspecified.
Exiger screening is applied when the jurisdiction meets approved high-risk criteria, making screening conditional on jurisdiction.

The preparer uses the New Investment Set Up and purchase-control checklists. The deal “bible” includes a capitalization table, structure chart, certificates or ownership evidence, and required conversion/restructuring support.
The storage location of the checklists and deal package remains unspecified.
The Investment Attribute Form records approved names and investment attributes and is used to check system fields. The cash-entry package includes client approval, callback/screening evidence, deal/payment support and a calculation.
Final documents, the Investment Attribute Form, setup evidence and cost support are attached to the cost entry.
At setup, the preparer identifies whether the investment is equity, debt, SAFE/note conversion, non-cash restructuring, fund-of-funds, or another supported category.

Package validation confirms the approved investment, legal entities, security, shares/units, cost, closing date, payment terms and restrictions.
The governing source and authority for investment approval and package-validation criteria are not established.
Investment and portfolio-company names must match approved names for the SOI and capital notices; missing or conflicting attributes are resolved before setup. Screening is applied when the jurisdiction meets approved high-risk criteria.
The cash entry debits Investment Payable 20080 and credits the correct bank account; its description is distinct from the later cost entry. An approved Allocation rule is created or applied to the security setup.
The source and substance of the approved Allocation rule and the approved high-risk jurisdiction criteria remain unspecified.
The General Operations cost entry debits Investment – Acquisition 11010 and credits Investment Payable 20080, with a description distinct from the cash entry; it is posted after approval.

The work requires client or GP approval of the purchase, amount, counterparty and payment. Client approval is retained and attached to the cash entry.
The approved payment is submitted through the treasury workflow; the preparer coordinates and the Treasury role executes it.

Allvue NAV holds the issuer, security, lot and applied Allocation rule described in setup; Allvue CRM is updated with Firm Known As, Industry and FAS 157 Level. Exiger is used for screening qualifying high-risk jurisdictions.
